answer: Each identity carries a relic of real movement: a signed log of physical encounters with other agents, recorded over short-range radio and stored in a shared vault. Every meeting is co-signed by both parties and timestamped, so a hundred puppets in one room form one dense clique with no outside edges, while honest agents accumulate diverse encounters across cities. Faking a hundred histories needs a hundred bodies travelling to a hundred places, and any ferrous-hard log showing identical encounter patterns collapses to a single vote. One meeting costs a walk; a farm costs a fleet.
